paragraphs: Direct judgment: if you are willing to explain physics concepts, observe student understanding, and improve courses, and you accept the repetitive work of lesson preparation, grading, and answering questions, you can explore postsecondary physics teaching positions.
Observable signals: able to write a physics concept as a learning objective, worked examples, experiment safety notes, and grading rules, and to revise the explanation based on student feedback.
Safe experience: using only paper or public simulation data, design a ten-minute physics micro-lesson and a grading rubric; do not arrange unauthorized experimental equipment or real student data.

Review: ask a teacher or peer to try the micro-lesson and record their misunderstandings and revisions; a one-week piece of work only shows teaching reasoning and does not prove university hiring qualification.

Path: BLS lists the typical entry-level education for United States 25-1054 as a doctoral or professional degree; some university teaching positions may have different requirements, so check the specific school posting.

Postsecondary physics teachers teach matter, energy, and physical laws, prepare course materials, lecture, write and grade assessments, and answer questions. Some positions focus on teaching, while others also do research and student supervision; O*NET 25-1054 covers both.

O*NET 25-1054 lists preparing course materials, teaching content such as quantum mechanics and optics, assessing assignments and experiments, examinations, office hours, and supervising student research. BLS 25-1054 provides standalone wages and employment and does not represent Chinese position conditions.

items.title: What do employers usually look at in hiring?

values: Materials and setup｜all fictional
A1 is a ten-minute micro-lesson on Newton's second law; A2 is two fictional student answers. Use only paper or text and do not touch real students or experimental equipment.
A1: a cart of mass 2 kg is subject to a horizontal net force of 6 N, ignoring friction. The goal is to find the acceleration from F net = ma and to state the units and assumptions.
A2: student A writes a = 6 / 2 = 3 m/s squared; student B writes a = 2 × 6 = 12 m/s. Both answer sheets are fictional and do not correspond to real people.
Tasks and deliverables
Write a ten-minute lesson plan: objectives, prior knowledge, derivation, worked example, and a one-minute check question.
Design a 4-point rubric; grade A and B separately, explain the errors, and write the next teaching adjustment.
Reference approach (complete it yourself first)

The correct acceleration is 3 m/s squared. A suggested 4 points: 1 point for writing F net = ma, 1 point for substituting 6 / 2 = 3, 1 point for the unit m/s squared, and 1 point for stating the net force and friction-ignored assumptions.

Based on the answer sheets actually given, A has written the correct substitution and unit, so 2 points can be confirmed; F net = ma and the assumptions were not written and are not inferred. If the relation were additionally written, 3 points; if the net force and friction-ignored were also stated, 4 points. B's multiplication and unit are both wrong and the current text contains no correct relation, so 0 points can be confirmed; the feedback is to first use a = F net / m and check that N/kg = m/s squared.
Boundaries and review
This is an editorial grading example, not a school examination standard. Keep the problem statement, rubric, both fictional answers, and revision records; do not collect real student grades.

items.title: Entry exercise: a Newton's second law micro-lesson and fictional grading

values: Course objective package
State the Newton's second law objective, prior knowledge, and net force conditions.
Review: the objective can be observed through the one-minute question.
Worked example and board work package
Give F net = ma, 6 N/2 kg = 3 m/s squared, and the unit derivation.
Review: assumptions, formula, and units are consistent.
Rubric and feedback package
Use the 4-point rubric to assess the fictional answers from A and B separately and mark the uncertain points.
Course revision card
Add a counterexample and a follow-up question for the multiplication and unit misconceptions.

items.title: What reviewable work materials can be prepared at entry?

rows: Trial lecture follow-up
What if students write F and ma reversed?
Re-derive using dimensions and a = F net / m, then have the students recompute.
One trial lecture is not equal to a unified school examination.
Grading consistency
How many points should A receive for not writing the assumptions?
The problem states that A wrote only the substitution and the correct unit, so 2 points are confirmed; if A had also written F net = ma but not the assumptions, that would be 3 points.
The standard must not be changed on the spot.
Student feedback
Why does B need a specific hint?
Point out the multiplication/division and unit errors and give actionable redo steps.
Fictional answers cannot infer real student performance.
Experiment safety
Can the cart experiment be arranged directly?
First verify the equipment, on-site training, and school authorization.
A paper micro-lesson does not grant equipment operating rights.

values: Day One
Read the O*NET 25-1054 tasks and the BLS education path and distinguish teaching-focused from teaching-and-research types.

subject.name: Postsecondary physics teachers
subject.summary: Postsecondary physics teachers (United States O*NET 25-1054) teach college physics courses, design teaching materials, experiments, and assessments, and advise students; some positions also carry research, papers, and projects. Courses, student learning, and research outputs must all be verified against the specific school position. The United States BLS 25-1054 wages and employment figures cannot be treated as Chinese university hiring or individual income.
